job.title: Strategic Advisor - Board Governance
job.description:
Our client is a leading, purpose-driven industry superannuation fund based in Melbourne, with a strong reputation for member-focused outcomes and a collaborative, values-driven culture. A high-impact 12-month project role has arisen for an experienced governance professional, supporting a high-functioning and well-respected Company Secretariat team.

Reporting to the Company Secretary and partnering with the Risk team to align governance and risk frameworks, you will provide specialist advice on the design and uplift of the fund's governance framework and processes, including an enhanced approach to Board and Committee capability assessment built around a skills matrix. The role involves assessing the current framework against better practice and evolving regulatory expectations, then developing the tools, templates and procedures that support lasting improvement. You will also partner with the business to deliver the uplift program.

You are a senior governance professional with experience in a governance, company secretarial, legal or risk function within a highly regulated environment (superannuation experience preferred but not essential). Degree qualified in Law, Business or a related field, you bring demonstrable experience in project execution and delivery. You will be trusted to deliver with a high level of independence and ownership, which will suit someone with a collaborative approach and the credibility to influence at Board and Executive level.

For a strictly confidential discussion, please contact Sarah Ling on 0402 265 217.  Alternatively, submit your application (Word version) via the Apply button.

job.title: Senior Finance Business Partner
job.description:
Dean & Ling Executive has been engaged exclusively to support one of Australia's leading manufacturing businesses that provides high-performance products and solutions for its blue-chip customer base in a critical sector globally.

As a Senior Finance Business Partner, you'll sit alongside the operational and commercial leaders and help them understand where performance stands, why it's happening, what's likely to happen next, and what to do about it.  Core accountabilities include:

  • Reporting and analysis: Deliver timely, accurate budgets, forecasts and month-end reporting across P&L, cash and working capital, linking financial outcomes to operational causes and leading performance reviews that drive action.
  • Commercial and contracts: Join key contract negotiations, build and manage Pricing Review Models, own customer rebates across the divisions, and assess the profitability impact of enterprise agreement proposals.
  • Inventory and controls: Make sure on-site, off-site and customer-located inventory is accurately accounted for and reconciled and investigate the root cause of significant or repeated variances.
  • Capital and compliance: Help prepare capital business cases, work with the FC on accounting standards, and support internal and external audits.
  • Insight and influence: Spot trends, recommend improvements and provide insight on cost, efficiency and commercial performance to shape decisions.
  • Leadership: Lead and develop a small team and take on other projects as needed.

What you'll bring

  • CA or CPA qualification with 10+ years' senior-level experience, ideally in a manufacturing-based business.
  • Strong accounting, financial management and reporting skills.
  • Advanced financial modelling, including experience developing standard costing and activity-based costing models.
  • Solid knowledge of cashflows, NPV and other valuation metrics.
  • Systems experience with Microsoft Dynamics D365 (or a similar ERP).
  • Excellent communication and negotiation skills, with the ability to influence and relate to all levels of management.
  • High attention to detail and the ability to work well under pressure.
  • A sound understanding of business and site processes.

For a strictly confidential discussion, please contact Ian Hackett on 0408 312 216.  Alternatively, submit your application (Word version) via the Apply button.

job.title: Director Operations
job.description:
At Central Highlands Regional Council, you'll have the opportunity to make a genuine and lasting impact on the communities, infrastructure and services that support one of Queensland's most diverse and significant regions.

Central Highlands Regional Council spans approximately 60,000 square kilometres, from Arcadia Valley in the south to the Peak Ranges in the north, and from Boolburra in the east to Bogantungan in the west. Managing more than $1.1 billion in community assets, Council delivers a diverse range of services through libraries, aquatic centres, customer service centres, 4,632 kilometres of roads, and extensive parks and recreational facilities.

This is an excellent opportunity to join a progressive regional Council. Home to nationally significant coal and energy operations, a strong agricultural sector and diverse regional communities, the Central Highlands plays a vital role in Queensland's economy and future growth.

Reporting to the Chief Executive Officer, the Director Operations is a key member of the Executive Leadership Team, responsible for shaping strategic direction, strengthening operational performance and driving organisational culture and excellence.

Working collaboratively across the organisation, you will lead a diverse portfolio encompassing infrastructure, project management, water utilities, parks and open spaces, and disaster management. You will champion a safety-first approach, fostering an accountable and high-performing culture, and driving continuous improvement in service delivery.

Key Responsibilities

  • Lead the delivery of Council's strategic and operational plans, budgets, policies and programs.
  • Contribute to enterprise strategy as a member of the Executive Leadership Team.
  • Develop long-term operational plans aligned with Council's vision and community objectives.
  • Manage budgets and business plans that support Council's Corporate Plan and financial sustainability.
  • Oversee major projects, ensuring delivery is achieved on time, within budget and to agreed standards.
  • Build strong relationships with government, industry, contractors and community stakeholders.
  • Provide visible leadership in workplace health, safety and risk management.
  • Promote a culture of accountability, collaboration, innovation and customer service.
  • Lead and inspire multidisciplinary teams to achieve high performance and continuous improvement.

The successful applicant will be a technically experienced executive leader with a track record of delivering results and leading teams in complex operational environments. They will be a visible, agile and credible leader who builds capability, inspires confidence and focuses on  strengthening safety performance.

You Will Bring

  • Proven leadership experience managing large multidisciplinary teams across infrastructure, engineering, works, asset management or related services.
  • Strong strategic planning and execution capability, with the ability to translate vision into measurable outcomes.
  • Tertiary qualifications in Civil Engineering, Business, Project Management or a related discipline.
  • Highly developed communication, negotiation and stakeholder management skills.
  • Strong commercial acumen, including budget, procurement and contract management experience.
  • The judgement and resilience to manage competing priorities in a dynamic and politically sensitive environment.


Why join CHRC?

This is more than an executive leadership role. It is an opportunity to influence the future of a region, deliver meaningful outcomes for communities, and lead large-scale projects and services that make a tangible difference every day.

Whether you're looking to grow your career, make a genuine impact, or achieve a better work-life balance, you'll find the opportunity at Central Highlands Regional Council. Join a team that supports your development, values your contribution, and helps you build the future you want.

  • Want a diverse and progressive career? Choose it here.
  • Ready to make real impact with people who care? Choose it here.
  • Looking for a better balance and the life you want? Choose it here.

If you are a collaborative and forward-thinking leader seeking the opportunity to leave a lasting legacy, we encourage you to apply.

For a strictly confidential discussion, please contact Ian Quinn or Mark Phillips at Dean & Ling Executive on 0414 609 604 or (07) 3211 1018. Alternatively, submit your application via the Apply button or visit www.deanling.com.au

Applications close midnight 28 October 2026.

For further information on Central Highlands Regional Council, visit www.chrc.qld.gov.au

job.title: Product & Regulatory Counsel
job.description:
Our client is a well-established, member-owned Australian financial services provider specialising in investment and insurance products. As trustee for a range of investment and savings vehicles, it prioritises socially responsible investing and long-term member outcomes. With growth ahead and a broader governance uplift under way, this is a genuine opportunity for a senior financial services lawyer to establish and maintain the function and make a real impact in this newly created part-time role.

Reporting to the CEO, you will provide practical legal advice on products, regulatory requirements, disclosure, complaints, contracts and governance. You will also maintain a clear and reliable record of key product requirements, legal interpretations and decisions. Working closely with stakeholders, you will advise on new product development, material product features, compliance, communication initiatives and broader commercial contracts.

You are a financial services lawyer with substantial post-admission experience, including significant time in an APRA-regulated business. You bring demonstrated expertise in Australian financial services regulation, the Corporations Act, and ASIC and APRA prudential standards, backed by sound knowledge of risk, compliance and governance. With sound judgement and strong drafting skills, you communicate persuasively, build strong relationships across the business and escalate material matters early. Pragmatic, commercially astute and risk-aware, you remain resilient as priorities change. This is a rare opportunity to shape the legal function of a purpose-led organisation, with the flexibility to work over three days or four shorter days.

For a strictly confidential discussion, please contact Sarah Ling on 0402 265 217.  Alternatively, submit your application (Word version) via the Apply button.

job.title: Senior Financial Accountant
job.description:
This is a rare opportunity to join a highly successful private enterprise which develops and manages a diverse portfolio of residential housing and community development projects across Australia. The business is managed by a highly experienced leadership team and maintains a values-driven, collaborative and down-to-earth workplace culture.

Reporting to the Chief Financial Officer, and as part of a small finance team, this broadly scoped role is primarily responsible for managing the periodic financial reporting, project accounting and all taxation compliance requirements for all entities within the Group. You will use your strong technical accounting skills to prepare accurate and timely monthly management reports, monitor and analyse cashflow and variances to budgets and forecasts and provide insightful analytical commentary to support operational decision making and business planning. You will be responsible for the preparation and lodgement of the annual income tax returns for all entities in the Group, and your detailed understanding of Australian Taxation compliance principles will be invaluable in ensuring that the enterprise continues to meet its periodic Indirect and Direct taxation compliance obligations. Additionally, you will help to coordinate the Group’s external accountants, tax advisors and auditors through the year end audit process and you will be expected to form collaborative working relationships with a broad range of internal and external stakeholders.

This is a broadly scoped and highly engaging role for a career minded CA/CPA qualified accounting professional now seeking the next step in their professional services career. You should possess demonstrable financial accounting expertise combined with a strong technical understanding of relevant Australian accounting and taxation principles, either gained in a Business Services & Tax environment or perhaps in a similar role in industry. Prior exposure to, or experience in, the property development sector is highly desirable. Previous experience with MYOB Advanced will also be well regarded.

For a strictly confidential discussion, please contact James McBeath on 0438 825 651.  Alternatively, submit your application (Word version) via the Apply button.

job.title: Security Coordinator
job.description:
South Bank Corporation is the renowned place manager behind Brisbane's premier recreational, cultural, educational and entertainment precinct, South Bank. With a vision to be a world-leading urban precinct that welcomes, engages and inspires, we are committed to innovating, managing and maintaining our enviable reputation while recognising the growing demand for green space in Brisbane's inner city.

The South Bank precinct spans 42 hectares, including 1.2 km of tree-lined riverfront and over 14 hectares of parkland, attracts 16.6 million people a year, hosts hundreds of events activities, supports over 9500 jobs and contributes over $2.4 billion to the Queensland economy.  

As Brisbane prepares to host Brisbane 2032, South Bank Corporation plays a pivotal role in ensuring our iconic precinct is ready to showcase Brisbane and Queensland on the world stage.

This key role as Security Coordinator is responsible for supporting security arrangements across protective, physical, and personnel security initiatives. You will work closely with the Security Manager and Security Supervisor to assist with public safety and facilities protection, whilst supporting customer experience, events, operations, and major contractors. 

As Security Coordinator, you will be responsible for the following;

  • Coordinating day-to-day physical security arrangements including access control, CCTV, keys, building security, and perimeter security, to ensure security is not compromised.
  • Coordinating the development of a Security Operations Manual and reviewing documentation and protocols, including a focus on at-risk people and customer-centric security arrangements. 
  • Contribute to the development, review, and continuous improvement of security policies, procedures, and standard operating guidelines.
  • Support protective security arrangements to ensure standards and expectations are met and collaborating closely with contractors to address issues.
  • Identifying security trends and issues from local, national, and international perspectives and escalating risks and concerns via Intelligence Bulletins and Security Briefs.
  • Assisting with incident investigations, including footage reviews, causal analysis, and developing mitigations, reports, and debriefs to close out incidents.
  • Supporting events via the preparation of Security Briefs and general event security planning to present for approval and endorsement
  • Preparing a security audit schedule and conducting audits on facilities and functions with internal stakeholders and presenting results for approval. 
  • Supporting customer experience teams and incident rooms during major events.
  • Liaison with internal and external stakeholders to support the overall security arrangements.
  • Participating in internal and external security precinct training exercises and coordinating forums, including logistical arrangements and preparation and circulation of minutes and debriefs.
  • Ensuring compliance with Australia’s Strategy for Protecting Crowded Places from Terrorism and relevant legislation. 
  • Supporting security culture and awareness campaigns.


Key Skills & Experience Required

  • Tertiary qualifications in criminology, justice studies, and/or intelligence are highly desirable.
  • Work experience as a security or intelligence professional in a similar environment with strategic and operational responsibilities is highly desirable
  • Working knowledge of crowded places security obligations and requirements, including Australia’s Strategy for Protecting Crowded Places from Terrorism.
  • Experience in developing procedures and protocols. 
  • Sound understanding of precinct security risks and threats.
  • Highly developed analytical, critical thinking and problem-solving skills and the ability to develop insights, identify trends and emerging issues, and communicate and disseminate advice.
  • Excellent liaison and negotiation skills demonstrated via experience dealing with law enforcement agencies and internal and external stakeholders from the Government, private sector, and community. 
  • Excellent oral, written, and interpersonal communication skills.
  • High level of integrity and professionalism demonstrated by experience in sensitive environments.
  • Demonstrated knowledge of physical and protective security systems relating to access control and surveillance, combined with a strong record of achievement.
  • This role may be required to work outside of normal business hours, including weekends.


If this sounds like your next career step, please contact Ian Quinn on 0403 343 097 for a strictly confidential discussion.  Alternatively, submit your application via the Apply button.

Closing date for applications is midnight 16 October 2026.
